correctness.rationale: Exact mod-two cyclic cancellation proves output parity. Unique 1001 antecedent for adjacent output ones gives seam-preserving period-n splicing. Binary XOR phase gives period-n or 2n antecedents for all cyclically isolated ones. These cases exhaust the image; weighted two-state transfer matrix proves the exact Lucas-minus-period-six-character count and rational generating function. Standalone exact checker validates n=1..12, 8190 words and 32760 assertions, without replacing the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Examined direct ECA rule18 image, evolution, periodic ring, weak-periodic-point and limit-set literature. Existing machinery and marker parity are acknowledged; none of the materially compared sources identified the combined explicit all-period exceptional-language characterization, Lucas/period-six count or sharp twofold lifting law. Substantive historical-priority risk persists because earlier automata could contain an implicit tabulation; this is not independent certification.

Salo and earlier studies establish the basic weak-periodic-point obstruction as a general concept; simple failure alone is not novel.
The 2023 Sabrié–Törmä marker parity argument can supply some of the local proof as prior art.
Complete scans of older finite-ring tables and early ECA formal-language theses were not possible; no independent priority assessment is claimed.

value.rationale: Periodic liftability is a natural symbolic-dynamical invariant used in cellular-automaton section/splitting problems. The all-period exact exceptional output language, its exponential Lucas census with a discrete period-six fluctuation, and sharp period-two lift for primitive outputs quantify a systematic finite-to-infinite discrepancy. The result is not a routine recalculation of an arbitrary sample: it completely classifies a canonical CA phenomenon, although the weak-periodic-point framework and underlying transfer method are established.
